author: reek
body: Browser-level event routing. Maps raw keyboard and mouse events to browser actions. Keyboard shortcuts follow standard browser conventions adapted for Codex.

author: reek
body: This chapter used to carry its own copy of the whole key table, in DOM codes, which is where `key-f5 = 116` came from and why plain `t` reloaded the page: 116 is also the letter. `UI chapter KeyInput` owns the named keys now, and a character is written as a character. There is one table.

author: reek
body: In the bare-metal environment, events come from the keyboard service (poll-key) and the kernel mouse module. poll-key returns a canonical key code as an Integer, or 0 if no key is pending, and `poll-mods` the held shift/ctrl/alt at that moment (the same bit values `mod-shift`/`mod-ctrl`/`mod-alt` above use). A letter is case-sensitive, so `map-ctrl-key` folds it through `key-upper` before matching a shortcut; the nav and function keys are DOM key codes used unchanged.

author: reek
body: For the MVP, we poll the keyboard. Mouse support requires the kernel Mouse module (PS/2 or USB HID).
